items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
COR-TRY-25-012, Tariff Update
notes:
Wayne Steffler, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, introduced the report, noting that it provides updates and outlines the risks posed by the tariffs.

In response to a question from the Committee regarding the new tax ratio in the province, W. Steffler explained that the adjustment applies to the aggregate property class. He noted that the change results in a lower tax rate for that class, which includes activities such as the extraction of materials from gravel pits. He clarified that while the overall tax revenue remains the same, the adjustment redistributes the tax burden across different property classes.

When asked why the tax ratio was lowered for the aggregate class, W. Steffler advised that the change was mandated by provincial legislation, and the Region was required to implement it.

J. Liggett requested that staff explore the possibility of a tax deferral and report back with additional information.

D. McCabe raised concerns about the Region’s critical infrastructure and the importance of ensuring access to necessary components through the procurement process. She inquired about the risks associated with supply chain issues, particularly regarding component parts, and asked what steps the Region is taking to mitigate those risks. She also asked about whether there is a need for provincial advocacy regarding what municipalities should or should not be purchasing. Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services, responded that the Region keeps critical and hard-to-source components on hand and is part of a network of municipalities that can support one another when needs arise. She added that, through the Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) process last year, the Region received approval for additional support related to securing essential components, particularly those connected to safeguarding the water supply. D. McCabe requested a follow-up email with further details.

items.title: Jonathan Walford and Kenn Norman, Fashion History Museum
notes:
J. Walford and K. Norman provided a presentation on the Fashion History Museum. A copy of the presentation is appended to the addendum agenda. They spoke about the various exhibitions and highlighted pieces from the museum’s collection.

items.title: Motions Where Notice Has Been Provided
Councillor D. Craig, Re: Fashion History Museum
notes:
D. Craig spoke to his motion, emphasizing his longstanding support for cultural enterprises. He requested that staff explore the possibility of working with the Fashion History Museum to determine how it could be more fully integrated into the community. He highlighted the museum’s unique and international contribution to the Region and expressed concern that its departure would represent a significant loss. He asked for the Committee’s support in advancing the motion.

During the discussion, Committee members expressed support for cultural institutions and the importance of doing what is possible to help organizations find a new home. Questions were raised about whether it is typical for the Region to assist in such situations, what staff resources would be required, and whether doing so would set a precedent.

In response, Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, explained that the Fashion History Museum’s collection falls outside the Region’s current collections policy, which focuses specifically on regional textile arts. He noted that supporting this initiative would not align with the Region’s core business and would have implications for existing work programs, including Council-directed initiatives such as the repositioning of the Region’s museums to support reconciliation and the management of archaeological resources. Preliminary discussions have taken place with the museum; however, the type of space they are seeking is not currently available. R. Regier added that while the museum has been previously funded through a grant program, that program is opening its next application round shortly and the museum is encouraged to apply.

Committee members acknowledged the cultural value of the museum but emphasized the importance of staying within the Region’s mandate. It was noted that the Region should not facilitate actions beyond its purview.

Responding to further questions, R. Regier confirmed that no support for the Fashion History Museum is included in the Region’s 2025–2026 business plan. J. Kingston, Director, Cultural Services, added that while it is common for Regional staff to provide professional advice to museum colleagues within Waterloo Region and across the province, it is not standard practice for the Region to take on more involved roles, such as scoping space needs or solving for collection storage and exhibition space. He also noted that although the Region has not previously seen multiple organizations partnering on grant applications, it is a possibility. The Fashion History Museum could explore this option independently, particularly in applying for key cultural institution funding with a partner organization.

Mathieu Goetzke, Acting Chief Administrative Officer, spoke from a staff perspective, emphasizing the operational impacts of pursuing this work. He noted that current staffing and resources are already stretched across multiple service areas, including time-intensive space-related initiatives. While the Museum’s needs are recognized, undertaking additional work would likely displace other high-priority initiatives. It was further emphasized that if this work were to proceed, timelines for other existing projects may need to shift into 2025.

motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to 2025 property tax policies and rates as set out in Report COR-CFN-25-005 dated April 8, 2025: Establish the following property class tax ratios for the 2025 property tax year: Residential and New Multi-residential 1.000000 Multi-residential, Commercial and Industrial 1.950000 Aggregate Extraction 1.586727 Landfill 1.540000 Pipeline 1.161300 Farmland and Managed Forest 0.250000 Direct staff to prepare the necessary by-laws to establish the 2025 property class tax ratios and the resulting 2025 Regional property tax rates for Regional Council’s consideration on April 23, 2025; and Notify the Area Municipalities within Waterloo Region accordingly.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to 2025 property tax policies and rates as set out in Report COR-CFN-25-005 dated April 8, 2025:

  1. Establish the following property class tax ratios for the 2025 property tax year:
    Residential and New Multi-residential 1.000000
    Multi-residential, Commercial and Industrial 1.950000
    Aggregate Extraction  1.586727
    Landfill 1.540000
    Pipeline 1.161300
    Farmland and Managed Forest 0.250000
  2. Direct staff to prepare the necessary by-laws to establish the 2025 property class tax ratios and the resulting 2025 Regional property tax rates for Regional Council’s consideration on April 23, 2025; and
  3. Notify the Area Municipalities within Waterloo Region accordingly.

motions.item_title: Councillor D. Craig, Re: Fashion History Museum
motions.text: Whereas The Fashion History Museum is ceasing operation in the City of Cambridge, And whereas its closure is a significant loss to the cultural fabric of the Regional community, And whereas the museum carries an international reputation with a collection that ranges from ancient Egyptian cloth to important couture like Dior, Chanel and Balenciagas, And whereas the museum in collaboration with the Historic School of Dress in London England is designing historic costumes for the Globe Theatre in London, And whereas the museum is partnering with a fashion designer in Antwerp who is showcasing items from the fashion museum to be shown at the Paris Fashion Week, Therefore be it resolved that the appropriate regional staff be requested to report on options to help promote the collection by partnering with other museums in the region and or securing space in an appropriate regional building or commenting on the possibility of a new stand-alone structure to service the whole regional community.
motions.text_html:
Whereas The Fashion History Museum is ceasing operation in the City of Cambridge,
 
And whereas its closure is a significant loss to the cultural fabric of the Regional community,
 
And whereas the museum carries an international reputation with a collection that ranges from ancient Egyptian cloth to important couture like Dior, Chanel and Balenciagas,
 
And whereas the museum in collaboration with the Historic School of Dress in London England is designing historic costumes for the Globe Theatre in London,
 
And whereas the museum is partnering with a fashion designer in Antwerp who is showcasing items from the fashion museum to be shown at the Paris Fashion Week,
 
Therefore be it resolved that the appropriate regional staff be requested to report on options to help promote the collection by partnering with other museums in the region and or securing space in an appropriate regional building or commenting on the possibility of a new stand-alone structure to service the whole regional community.
